name: Kee-po-tah, at the gathering of August 1812

review_note: review_required: a Potawatomi person of the gathering at Chicago in August 1812, the eve of the battle in which the garrison and its families were attacked. The card states only what the named sources say, says where a story is Kinzie family tradition rather than a contemporary account, and stages no speech or ceremony.

not_in_this_household.note: No source names his family or places his lodge in the camp.

persons.name: Kee-po-tah

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the afternoon of 14 August 1812, read from the evidence below; no source takes a roll call that afternoon.

persons.note: Chief; Kinzie family's protector. Potawatomi (band not stated; with To-pee-nee-bee at St Joseph in autumn 1812). Guarded the Kinzie boat at the river mouth on the morning of the 15th (Wau-Bun), so very likely at Chicago on the 14th. 15 and 16 August: Protected Mrs Kinzie's boat; sentinel on the 16th; escorted the family to Detroit in November 1812; had met Harrison at the 1811 Vincennes council. Afterwards: With the Kinzies at Detroit, autumn 1813 (Wau-Bun ch. XX).
